patent_grounding.rationale: Revision 3 removes the standalone F_FORCE flow that was not connected to any port/interface. The remaining P_FORCE_IN is explicitly a system-boundary input port (mechanical_force), not a claimed force-source component or internal force-transformation flow. Patent claims 4–5 expressly mention externally applied force; claims 1–2 support the cell, layers, overlapping side members, flexures, plate segments and nodes. Force remains accurately represented as an input, not as an invented actuator.

functional_completeness.rationale: Core claimed elements and functions remain represented: compliant flexures, overlapping plate/shell barrier segments, shape deformation, contiguous line-of-sight barrier, guided motion, and return tendency after force removal. Claim-dependent edge and return features are appropriately qualified. Removal of F_FORCE does not omit the force input because P_FORCE_IN remains.

flow_consistency.rationale: The previously disconnected item-flow object is absent, resolving REV2-1. The externally applied force is represented by the input boundary port and its mechanical_force type, without an unsupported standalone flow association. F_MOTION is referenced by the SURF-to-PLATE interface and the paired motion ports have compatible mechanical_motion types and directions.

claim_traceability.rationale: Claims and descriptive passages cited for the modeled mechanisms, force response, barrier, boundary behavior and return tendency are textually supportive. Claim-specific requirements retain their claim numbers and dependent-claim qualification.

interfaces.rationale: The SURF-to-PLATE motion interface connects existing compatible output/input ports once. No external source subsystem is fabricated. P_FORCE_IN correctly remains a boundary port rather than a subsystem-to-subsystem interface; patent text does not identify an external force source.

textbook_application.rationale: The retrieved context/interface guidance supports distinguishing system boundary from environment and modeling relevant entities crossing that boundary. This justifies treating applied force as an external boundary input, but is not used as evidence for patent facts. SJS modeling guidance also supports preserving meaningful input/output relationships.

summary: Revision 3 resolves the prior disconnected F_FORCE finding: the orphan item flow has been removed while the supported externally applied force remains represented by SURF.P_FORCE_IN (direction in, flow_type mechanical_force). This is a suitable boundary-port representation and does not require inventing a force-source component or unsupported interface. No new material issues identified in the reviewed SJS.
